story.head: Reinhart’s favorite opponent
paras: The Islanders (12-8-5) lost 3-1 to Winnipeg on Friday, while the Panthers have won three straight. Going in, the Panthers are second in the Atlantic (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Islanders third in the Metropolitan (17th).
The Panthers’ record (.635) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.580) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

This season, the Panthers have outscored teams 84-76, even though they’ve been outscored 50-44 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 26-18, and only one team creates more chances on the power play.

The Panthers forecheck harder than anyone (1st) and rarely ice the puck (1st), but don’t block many shots (32nd). On the other side, the Islanders roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). The Cats’ power play (3rd) could do real damage against the Islanders’ penalty kill (29th), though their penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way. Beyond that, the Islanders have the edge over the Panthers on shots from defensemen.

Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 28 A / 35 P in 26 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is sixth in the NHL, with seven goals in seven games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Sam Reinhart (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 26 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 25 GP) has a team-high ten goals.
Jacob Markström (9-4-1 / .895 SV% in 15 GS) is in line to start for Florida. Ilya Sorokin (10-5-2 / .916 SV% in 17 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and will likely start.
